incident-bot: ALERT 7043219999 — Dedicated pool eu-west-1 (gpu-p4) p99 latency breach detected
incident-bot: metrics: p95=420ms p99=2.8s, streaming stalls increased, queue depth trending up > 1200
incident-bot: severity: P1, paging on-call

sam: acked — joining. seeing alerts in grafana too: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west1/dedicated/pool-latency
sam: oncall in the last 5m: scale ops spikes + warmup latency. probably autoscaler slow to hand off new slots

ops-bot: runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-pool-sat
ops-bot: suggested immediate actions: 1) hand-scale pool +1 2) route hotshot traffic away 3) reduce batch size for streaming routes

priya: adding telemetry snippet from runtime logs (last 3 mins):
```
[2026-03-15T08:58:21Z] pool=eu-west-1 id=pool-42 queue_depth=1267 warmup_inflight=32 autoscale_request=+8 pending_slots=0
[2026-03-15T08:58:22Z] model=redwood-2q seq=1024 kv_miss=true stream_chunk_hang=45ms
[2026-03-15T08:58:25Z] handshake=delayed by 1.2s for new slot allocation
```
priya: note: warmup_inflight high and pending_slots 0 — autoscaler is requesting nodes but handshake/slot provisioning delayed (cloud provider side?).

leo: are we certain it's provider-side or internal warmup (nfs / model load)? any OOMs in node logs?

priya: checked node logs: no OOMs. model load time is elevated for large seq lengths (1k+). trace shows kernel selection thrash on new instances, causing warmup to stall ~1-1.5s per slot. autoscaler thinks slots ready but runtime still finishing warmup (kv cache priming).

maya: I'm taking page — oncall (maya) live. leaving note for handoff: 1) manual scale +4 for pool-42, 2) set priority queue threshold to 30% for hotshot tiers, 3) enable fallback variant v2-quantized for streaming endpoints. will coordinate with infra and support.
maya: paging PD on infra: @leo @sam @priya — pls standby for live ops, leaning on manual scale and redispatch.

leo: starting manual scale now — calling autoscaler API to force pool +4 (temp).
leo: command: ```curl -XPOST https://controlplane.redwood/api/pools/pool-42/scale -d '{"desired": 42}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN'```
leo: submitted. cloud provider reports new instances provisioning (3/4 ready)

ops-bot: scaling action recorded, pool desired=42 -> 46, timestamp 7043219965

maya: while instances spin up — reducing streaming batch size on route `/v1/stream/chat` to 8 -> 4 to cut tail latency. applying partial config:
```
PATCH /config/routes/stream-chat
{ "batch_size": 4, "priority": "realtime" }
```
maya: applied, pushing traffic change to edge.

priya: early telemetry after batch size change (~30s): p95 dropped to ~310ms, p99 still ~1.9s. queue depth down 18% from peak but streaming stalls still observed as new slots join and finish warmup.

sam: customer-impact check: CS flagged 2 customers complaining — ACME-search (streaming) and NovaAnalytics (async gen). ACME reports intermittent truncated streams and 502 spikes ~08:56-09:02 UTC.

customer-success: ACME seeing 40% of streaming sessions show stream-cut (client-side) with reconnects. logs show server hang then 502. NovaAnalytics seeing increased latency but no errors yet.

maya: prioritizing ACME as they are on dedicated SLA. immediate mitigation: route ACME traffic to fallback pool eu-west-1-fallback (smaller models, lower perf but stable). will update routing policy to pin ACME to fallback for next 15m.

leo: routing change command (controlplane):
```
POST /controlplane/routing/override
{"customer_id":"acme", "target_pool":"eu-west-1-fallback", "ttl":900}
```
leo: change applied. routing propagate ~25s.

priya: observing ACME session stream: error rate dropped to ~9% after reroute. good. overall p99 for pool-42 continues to improve as slots finish warmup and kv priming completes.

maya: next steps: 1) keep manual scale until autoscaler heals 2) open cloud ticket with provider (VM warmup high) — @sam can you open? 3) schedule follow-up postmortem.
maya: assigning action owners: provider ticket -> sam, postmortem -> priya, customer comms -> customer-success. please ack.

sam: opened provider ticket #PROV-8897 with logs and warmup timestamps. added priority.

leo: autoscaler watchdog shows backlog cleared: pending_slots=0, warmup_inflight tapering to 3, queue_depth at ~220. p99 now 680ms.

ops-bot: incident-bot update: severity degraded P2 — customer impact contained for ACME via reroute. continuing monitoring for 30m.

maya: I'm going to hand off to oncall for monitoring window. leaving notes: - watch p99 and queue depth - watch for handshake errors - keep ACME pinned until next sync - communicate to support to notify ACME of temporary reroute (CS).

priya: preliminary root cause hypothesis: dedicated pool hit cold-model warmup thrash when autoscaler added many slots under burst load; runtime kernel selection + kv priming created additional warmup latency causing effective capacity lower than autoscaler expected -> queue buildup -> tail stalls. mitigation: staggered slot warmup, pre-warm for large-seq customers, and improve autoscaler to wait for runtime-ready signal (not just VM up).

customer-success: notifying ACME now: "We've routed your streaming workloads to a fallback pool to restore stability. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with timeline and mitigation."

maya: handoff complete to monitoring oncall (leo). leaving channel.

leo: acked. monitoring for 30m. will open postmortem doc now: https://wiki.redwood/postmortems/7043219999-dedicated-saturation-runtime-triage

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE 7043220100 — monitoring window started, contact list updated, incident state: under-observation

(threads end)
